title: Change Employers for Career Progress, Workers Say
paragraphs: Many workers believe that the best way to move up in their careers is to leave their current company, according to a new study.

The research, called "Talent Mobility at Work in 2026," was carried out by SHL, a company that specializes in assessing workers' skills. It surveyed more than 2,000 working adults in the US and the UK.

The study found that 66% of workers think they need to change employers in order to advance. Many of them feel that their companies do not give them enough chances to grow. For example, 59% of US workers and 49% of UK workers said their employer prefers to hire people from outside the company rather than promote existing staff.

Workers also gave other explanations. About 31% said managers do not want to lose good employees. In addition, 54% said they had been passed over for a role because they did not have a certain degree or qualification, and another 21% suspected this had happened to them. Perhaps for this reason, 61% said employers should stop requiring degrees for most jobs.

However, the survey also suggests that many workers would be happy to stay if they had more opportunities. Around 84% said they want their employer to show them internal jobs that match their skills. Meanwhile, 83% said they would be willing to retrain for a more senior position, and 89% said they would take a skills test to show what they can do.

Managers may not fully understand their workers' abilities, either. Although 83% of workers said their manager knows about skills they have beyond their current job, only 42% said those skills are fully understood.
Lucy Beaumont, a senior vice president at SHL, said that the biggest missed opportunity for business leaders today is overlooking the talent they already have.
